data.one_liner: Support iOS Live Activities, Android RemoteViews and Dynamic Island.
data.what_it_does: Enables Flutter apps to display and update iOS Live Activities, the Dynamic Island, and Android RemoteViews. It bridges Dart data with native Swift (ActivityKit) and Kotlin UI implementations.
use_when: You need to show live status updates on the iOS lock screen or Dynamic Island.
You want to display ongoing persistent notifications on Android using RemoteViews.
avoid_when: You only need standard push or local notifications without live updating widgets.
You cannot write native Swift and Kotlin code for the UI extensions.
strengths: Brings native iOS Live Activities and Android RemoteViews to Flutter.
Allows custom activity tagging and state management.
weaknesses: Requires significant native configuration and UI development in Swift and Kotlin.
Only works on iOS 16.1+ and Android API level 24+.
data.setup_notes: Requires creating a Widget Extension in Xcode, configuring App Groups and Push Notifications capabilities in iOS, and implementing custom Java/Kotlin classes and XML layouts for Android RemoteViews.
